title: Serve bee blind check and refuse a malformed dossier by section name
verify: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml verbs::blind && PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml catalog && PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml --test registry_dispatch --test registry_contracts
action:
Serve `bee blind check --dossier <path>`: the one new verb decision f0f21142 allows. This cell delivers the verb, its namespace wiring, the dossier's fixed section contract, and a re-run of bln-2's brief guard over the dossier's recorded brief. The three EVIDENCE checks (citations, digest equality, read diet) are bln-4 — do not build them here.

Copy the shape of an existing small namespace: `packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/triggers/mod.rs` is 728 lines with `pub fn try_native` at :352 and its own inline `mod tests` at :501-727. Follow it.

WIRING — a new top-level namespace is invisible to more checks than a new sub-verb, so all four land here:
1. `verbs/mod.rs` — declare `pub mod blind;` beside its siblings and add `if let Some(code) = blind::try_native(args, t0) { return Some(code); }` to the probe chain that starts at `pub fn try_native` (:47). Help probes stay FIRST; put the new arm with the other verb groups, not before them.
2. `router.rs` — add `"blind check"` to the `PORTED` list (the doc comment at :24 says keep it in sync with the probes).
3. `src/generated/registry_payload.json` — hand-edit. `bee dev regen` does NOT write this file. Declare `blind.check` with a runnable `examples[0]`: `tests/registry_dispatch.rs` executes every entry's first example against the built binary, so the example must succeed on a dossier this repo actually has — ship one under `docs/history/slp-blind-lanes/blind/` as the example's target, or make the example a refusal the runner accepts.
4. `tests/registry_dispatch.rs` — the served-but-undeclared law at `every_namespace_the_dispatcher_serves_is_declared_in_the_registry` (:400) scans exactly three tables (`devtools/mod.rs`, `herding.rs`, `served_cells_verbs()`) plus two bare probes, and would NOT see `bee blind` at all. Add a scanner arm for it, the same shape as the `bee dev` and `bee herding` arms. Without this, a served-and-undeclared blind sub-verb would ship silently and read as unknown to `bee --help --all`.
5. `catalog.rs` — bump `PINNED_FLAG_COUNT`, which bln-1 already moved to 197 and now sits at `catalog.rs:649` (the line MOVED from 632, so search for the constant, never the old number). Carry the written reuse check the ledger comment demands. Address `--file` (six uses), `--dossier` is new; say why `--file` was not reused (it names a payload path on commands that CONSUME the file's content as input to a write; blind check reads a document as evidence and writes nothing).

THE DOSSIER CONTRACT — the fixed sections plan.md locks, in order: `# Blind lane run <run-id>`, `## Question`, `## Lanes` (one `### <lane-id>` each, carrying its `dispatch_id`, its `brief_sha256`, its role, its paths read, and the proposal verbatim), `## Cross-critiques`, `## Chosen`, `## Rejected`, `## Citations`, `## Revisit trigger`. A missing, extra or misordered section REFUSES BY NAME of the offending section — never by silently checking less. Copy the refusal shape from `unmapped_kind_refusal` (drivers/prepare.rs:56-69): {ok:false, type:"refused", reason, ..., fix}.

THE LINT RE-RUN — call `lint_brief` from `verbs/drivers/brief_lint.rs` over the brief the dossier records under `## Question`, so a convergence built on an unlinted brief refuses. That is the second caller the bln-2 cell exposed the function for; do not copy its stem list, and author the test that asserts both callers use the one function (a rule living in n places needs one test that reads all n).

Tests — put them in an inline `mod tests` INSIDE `verbs/blind/mod.rs` so the verify filter `verbs::blind` actually matches them. bln-2 shipped a verify half filtering on `brief_lint` that matched ZERO tests and still exited green; if you place tests anywhere else, change the verify line and record the deviation. Author: each section arm red-first (missing, extra, misordered, no headings at all), a lane section missing its dispatch_id or brief_sha256 refusing by name, a well-formed dossier passing, and the shared-lint test.

truths: bee blind check --dossier <path> is served by the binary and declared in the registry, so bee --help --all lists it

A dossier whose recorded brief carries leaning language is refused by the same guard the dispatch door uses
A well-formed dossier passes this cell's checks
The served-but-undeclared law now scans the blind namespace, so a future undeclared sub-verb fails the suite

Both 'the plan was wrong about a fact' deviations are genuinely FORCED, not convenience. (a) brief_lint.rs:221-232 hard-refuses any brief missing one of the four BRIEF_SECTIONS, so a Question-only recording would refuse every dossier - whole-brief recording is required by the plan's own lint-re-run, and bln-4's digest check needs those bytes. (b) Proposals are stored verbatim and are arbitrary prose, so without the fence mask a quoted '## Chosen' inside a proposal would become a section boundary; pinned by mod.rs:930-940.
